response.passage: The Mauryan Empire was established by Chandragupta Maurya, who was guided by a brilliant advisor named Chanakya. Their capital city was Pataliputra. One of the most famous rulers of this dynasty was Ashoka. Early in his reign, Ashoka fought a brutal war against the kingdom of Kalinga. This was a massive, bloody conflict that changed his life forever. After seeing the destruction, Ashoka decided to stop fighting and instead promoted a set of moral principles called Dhamma. Dhamma was not a religion, nor was it forced upon his people; it was a way of living based on kindness, tolerance, and respect for others. To share his message, Ashoka had his teachings carved into hard stone pillars and rock surfaces. These inscriptions were permanent records meant for the public to read, as paper was not used for such royal proclamations during that time. Through these stone messages, Ashoka encouraged his subjects to live in peace and harmony, showing that a ruler could lead through compassion rather than just military force.
response.summary: Chandragupta Maurya founded the empire with Chanakya's help, while Ashoka later transformed his rule after the Kalinga war. Ashoka spread his moral teachings, known as Dhamma, by carving them onto stone pillars for his people to read.
